skills.name: agent-skill-creator
skills.description: Guide for creating, structuring, and organising AI agent skills — building a skill from scratch, setting up a .agents/ workspace, designing folder structures, and writing SKILL.md files with proper YAML frontmatter.
skills.content: Defines skill structure levels (single-file vs. multi-file with references vs. full workspace), when to use each, a quick-reference for frontmatter fields and folder layout, a how-to-use flow, and a link to the full reference document covering AGENT.md and agent rules/context.

skills.name: agentic-engineering
skills.description: Turns a one-line request into a brief an AI coding agent can execute without drifting. Applies four framing questions — what is being created, for whom, what are the limitations, how will it be proven complete and correct — then interrogates for the unstated rules (expiry, reuse, rate limits, concurrency, failure paths) that decide whether generated code is right or merely plausible.
skills.content: A five-step method: frame with the four questions, interrogate the answers against seven question banks (lifetime/reuse, volume/abuse, identity/permission, state/concurrency, failure/recovery, data lifecycle, integration) plus domain add-ons, write a one-page brief with numbered rules, prohibitions and proofs, confirm it, then build against it. Includes an adjective-to-limitation conversion table, a brief template, a full worked example (password reset from one sentence to ten proof lines), and rules for what counts as proof of done versus theater.

skills.name: ai-web-product-craft
skills.description: Guidance for web pages and apps that load images/iframes/embeds and/or include an AI feature (chatbot, agent, summarizer, recommender, generative UI). Combines HTML delivery performance (TTFB, caching, compression, CDNs, lazy loading, embed facades) with responsible AI product design (privacy, fairness, calibrated trust, AI UX pattern choice).
skills.content: Three parts plus a combined checklist: (1) HTML and resource-loading performance — TTFB, caching, compression, CDN, lazy loading images and iframes, third-party embed facades; (2) building AI features responsibly — privacy, fairness, transparency, calibrated trust, governance; (3) choosing the right AI UX pattern — background, constrained, or open-ended. Ends with a shipping checklist for putting an AI feature inside a normal page, and sources.

skills.name: clean-code-javascript
skills.description: Clean Code principles and best practices for JavaScript/TypeScript. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring JS/TS to improve readability, maintainability, and correctness — naming, function design, class structure, SOLID, error handling, testing patterns, formatting.
skills.content: Clean Code rules grouped into priority categories (naming, functions, objects/classes, SOLID, concurrency, error handling, comments, testing) with a quick-reference cheat sheet, guidance on which categories to apply for a given task, and a link to the full compiled reference.

skills.name: cs-course-designer
skills.description: Research, plan, and write course/unit outlines, Course Learning Outcomes (CLOs), lesson/teaching plans, and assessments (quizzes, exams, rubrics, project briefs) for general CS, DBMS, SQL, Python, and C. Also reviews existing CLOs, lesson plans, and assessments for alignment. Not for other languages or live 1:1 tutoring.
skills.content: Scoped, scaled workflow: understand the task, research subject scope, plan structure, write measurable CLOs, then build teaching/lesson plans (objectives, prior knowledge, materials, warm-up, direct instruction, guided practice, independent lab) and aligned assessments. Adapts depth to audience level (university, bootcamp, high school, professional) and request size — a single CLO gets a direct answer, a full course gets the full pipeline.

skills.name: css-architecture
skills.description: Scaffold and manage CSS file architecture for TailwindCSS-first projects. Use to organize CSS files, prevent or fix 'CSS hell', add custom styles alongside Tailwind, set up structural design tokens, configure PostCSS imports, enforce lint rules, or migrate a messy stylesheet.
skills.content: Starts with a mandatory intake step, then applies the Golden Rule (Tailwind first, custom CSS only for what utilities can't express). Defines a standard styles/ folder structure, CSS cascade layers as the core conflict-prevention tool, structural design tokens in tokens/_root.css, Tailwind config alignment, a workflow for adding new styles, PostCSS setup for @import, an anti-pattern table, a QA validation checklist, and success metrics.

skills.name: data-analyze
skills.description: Answer data questions end-to-end, from a quick metric lookup to multi-dimensional analysis to a formal report. Triggers on any request that requires querying, aggregating, or interpreting data from a warehouse, table, CSV/Excel, or pasted results.
skills.content: Six-step pipeline: classify the question (lookup vs. investigation vs. report), gather data (connected warehouse or user-provided files), analyze, validate before presenting (sanity-check aggregations and assumptions), present findings in the right format (number, table, chart, narrative), and visualize only where it adds meaning.

skills.name: debug-master
skills.description: Deep debugging and auto-fix across file system inspection, logic and workflow tracing, and algorithm analysis. Triggers on any error message, stack trace, broken path, missing module, wrong output, or vague "something is wrong" report. Covers Python, JS/TS, Go, Bash, SQL, and agent workflows (LangChain/LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI).
skills.content: Four-phase pipeline — Inspect, Isolate, Diagnose, Fix — with an intake phase that extracts what is needed from vague reports. Includes file-system checks, state-flow tracing for long chains, complexity and edge-case analysis, and a verify step that patches, tests, and guards.

skills.name: deploy-to-vercel
skills.description: Deploy applications and websites to Vercel. Use for requests like 'deploy my app', 'push this live', 'give me the link', or 'create a preview deployment'.
skills.content: Gathers project state (framework, git status, existing Vercel link), chooses a deploy method (CLI, git push, or dashboard), handles agent-specific constraints, reports the resulting deployment URL, and includes a troubleshooting section for common build and linking failures.

skills.name: flutter
skills.description: Flutter/Dart application engineering — architecture, layout debugging, responsive design, and widget previews. Triggers on 'structure my Flutter project', 'RenderFlex overflowed', 'unbounded height viewport', 'make this responsive', 'add a widget preview', and similar.
skills.content: A router skill: identifies which Flutter concern the request touches and directs work to focused reference guides under refer/ (architecture, layout errors, responsive design, previews), plus a short working protocol for how to apply them.

skills.name: frontend-design
skills.description: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one — aesthetic direction, typography, and choices that don't read as templated defaults.
skills.content: Grounds design decisions in the subject matter rather than generic templates. Covers core design principles, a process of brainstorm → explore → plan → critique → build → critique again, the role of restraint and self-critique, and writing as a design element (copy, tone, typographic voice).

skills.name: github-report
skills.description: Turn GitHub activity — commits, pull requests, and issues — into a written report (.md) of completed work, grouped by sprint, feature, function, or section. Also defines the commit, PR, and issue conventions that make such a report possible.
skills.content: Two halves: the conventions that make history machine-readable, and the report built from it. Starts with a ground-truth check on git log to decide whether grouping will be reliable or inferred, pins scope (window as absolute dates, repo/branch, grouping axis, audience) before collecting, then collects via git and gh and writes the .md. Warns explicitly when conventions are absent rather than inventing structure the data does not contain.

skills.name: google-design-system
skills.description: Apply Google Design principles across 16 domains: Material 3 Expressive, motion design, Google Sans Flex typography, AI/Gemini visual design, global accessibility, design sprints, UX writing, brand building, design culture, and XR/AI glasses (Glimmer). Use for any task involving Google design standards.
skills.content: Written partly in Thai. Provides a quick reference to read first, a domain map pointing to the right reference file per topic, a step-by-step usage flow, a recommended output format, a senior design leadership review pass, and official Google source URLs.

skills.name: java-api-performance
skills.description: Java Spring Boot backend API performance optimization. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Java/Spring Boot code to fix slow APIs, memory issues, or database inefficiencies — loop optimization, caching, pagination, query tuning, N+1 problems, indexing, async processing, connection pooling (HikariCP).
skills.content: Nine copy-ready BAD vs BETTER patterns for the most common Spring Boot performance killers, ordered by priority (N+1 queries, missing indexes, unbounded result sets, caching, async, pooling). Includes a quick-reference table, when-to-apply triggers, and a link to the full compiled reference document.

skills.name: knowledge-base
skills.description: Software engineering knowledge base covering architecture patterns, component-based design, security fundamentals, software design principles, and use case + microservices design. Use when answering architecture, design pattern, system design, security, or use-case modeling questions.
skills.content: Indexes several knowledge domains (architecture patterns and 3-tier design, component-based design, security fundamentals, design principles, use case modeling and microservices) into a quick-reference, with routing to the matching reference file for depth.

skills.name: lighthouse
skills.description: Diagnose and fix a website to earn high Lighthouse scores across Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices, SEO, and Agentic Browsing on both desktop and mobile. Triggers on shared Lighthouse/PageSpeed/Core Web Vitals reports or failing metrics (FCP, LCP, TBT, CLS, INP, Speed Index).
skills.content: Operating principle: diagnose before touching code, then run a measure → fix → re-measure loop. Defines score targets, triages where points actually are, and gives per-category playbooks (performance first as the biggest lever, then accessibility, best practices, SEO, agentic browsing). Treats desktop and mobile as separate targets, includes framework quick-notes, a verification gate as the definition of done, and an anti-pattern list.

skills.name: long-horizon-engineering-workflow
skills.description: A six-stage gated delivery workflow (Requirements → Design → Development → QA → UAT → Deployment) to keep long, multi-session, or multi-stage builds from drifting. Use for any 'build me X' request too big for one shot; not for snippets or small well-specified fixes.
skills.content: Two loops: a gated outer loop (Requirements → Design → Development → Integration QA → UAT → Deployment) around a per-feature inner loop that runs scoped regression → select → implement → verify → refactor what that feature touched → ledger → commit, backed by four harness files at the repo root (build-spec.md, feature-list.json, progress.md, init script) so state survives context loss. The refactor box is bounded to the feature's own diff, forbidden from changing behaviour, and re-verified against the same steps — which is what keeps a build that passes every gate from degrading one commit at a time. Stage 2 runs computational thinking as its method — decomposition into the feature ledger, pattern recognition for reuse, abstraction for the interface contract, algorithm design branch by branch, and data mapping at every boundary. Operates in 'strong push' mode requiring gate artifacts before advancing while respecting explicit overrides, and holds twelve hard invariants including an append-mostly ledger and never claiming an unobserved pass.

skills.name: obsidian-vault
skills.description: Turn an Obsidian vault into a persistent, self-organizing knowledge base that Claude Code reads from and writes to across sessions — second brain / PKM setup, ingesting documents, URLs and transcripts into linked notes, querying past notes, and running project wikis.
skills.content: Defines the core idea of a durable cross-session knowledge store, a vault layout, note conventions (frontmatter, links, tags), the supported operations (/vault, /ingest, /wiki — setup, ingest, query, update), a hot cache format for fast recall, cross-project referencing rules, and guardrails on what to write and what to leave out.

skills.name: owasp-top-10-2025
skills.description: Security review and vulnerability analysis based on the OWASP Top 10 2025. Use when auditing code for security flaws, reviewing authentication, checking for injection, or ensuring cryptographic correctness — broken access control, misconfiguration, vibe-coding risks, memory management, supply chain, resilience failures.
skills.content: Organizes the 2025 Top 10 into vulnerability categories ordered by severity, with a quick reference for what to look for per category, a how-to-use flow for running a review, and reference files with detailed detection patterns and remediations.

skills.name: project-file-structure
skills.description: Rules for naming and placing every file and folder in a React + TypeScript + Node + Prisma project whose documentation lives in an Obsidian vault, plus PDF handling. Applies when creating, renaming, or moving any file, writing a Prisma model or migration, adding a vault note, or reviewing a PR that adds files.
skills.content: Three governing rules — case is correct, files of one feature stay connected, and a name is findable in 10 seconds — expanded into naming tables per file type (components, pages, hooks, utils, types, routes, controllers, services, repositories, tests, PDF templates and generated PDFs), Prisma model and migration conventions, feature-folder colocation, and Obsidian vault note placement with links back to the code they describe.

skills.name: promethean-parthenon
skills.description: The operating doctrine for getting high-performance output out of an AI coding agent, and the router across the five skills that produce it, organised as Role · Task · Format: set the seat that answers (senior-leadership-advisor), write the target and build against it (requirement-gathering, agentic-engineering, long-horizon-engineering-workflow), and land the result in a record built from real data (github-report).
skills.content: Three pillars — Role, Task, Format — with a load path where each hands the next a written artifact. Task is the widest, carrying three skills and one ordering rule: you cannot build against a target you have not written down, so extract it with requirement-gathering when it lives in code, brief it with agentic-engineering when it lives in someone's head, then build against it under gates. Provides a routing table (by what you hold, by what went wrong, and sized to the work), the five levers that actually change agent output quality ranked by effect (target specificity, verification actually run, state outliving the conversation, effort placed at decisions, scope held still), a catalogue of fourteen silent failure modes with their tells and cheapest detection, and explicit hand-offs to skills outside the set.

skills.name: requirement-gathering
skills.description: Autonomous requirement extraction and documentation for PERN/MERN full-stack projects with micro design standards — the 'extract' skill of the Promethean Parthenon Task pillar, for when requirements live in code rather than in someone's head. Produces a complete Markdown requirements document without asking follow-up questions. Thai triggers included (วิเคราะห์ code, เขียน spec, ทำ requirements, audit component).
skills.content: Runs an autonomous protocol: auto-detect context, then emit layered contracts — frontend component contract (always), API contract, DB schema contract — followed by functional requirements, non-functional requirements, a lean risk register, and a small-team sign-off checklist. Ends with a full output document template; missing context is inferred and annotated as assumptions rather than asked about.

skills.name: security

skills.content: Architecture references for OAuth2 flows and leveled API keys (read-only / write / admin scoping), agent-to-service security design, a threat response playbook for key compromise and rotation, a security review checklist, a decision matrix for choosing between patterns, and a list of red flags to always call out.

skills.name: senior-leadership-advisor

Includes worked examples of the voice.

skills.name: skill-creator

skills.content: Ten-part reference: connection reference card (pooler vs. direct), RLS architecture rules, Prisma ↔ Supabase schema design rules, a Postgres → Supabase migration playbook, a workflow and logic checker, an algorithm reviewer, patterns for Supabase-backed AI agents, Realtime + Prisma coexistence, advisor-mode senior recommendations, and a quick command reference.

skills.name: tracking-and-debugging
